section_summary: This section finishes a translated Japanese foreign exchange control ordinance, covering overseas property, remittances, trade payments, exchange businesses, inspections, and reporting. It then begins selected articles of Japan’s 1940 Income Tax Law, including taxable income, rates, deductions, declarations, and the election and operation of Income Investigation Committees.

people.name: V. J. Sebald
people.role: Translator of the cited Civil Code of Japan

subfiles.title: Foreign exchange control ordinance of Japan (conclusion)
subfiles.about: Concluding provisions regulate overseas assets and payments, foreign trade, exchange businesses, inspections, permits, and reports.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance requires permits or reports for dealings in overseas property, repatriation of proceeds and profits, export and import payments, and foreign exchange transactions. It sets rules for exchange banks, money changers, and brokers, and grants the Finance Minister inspection and special order powers. Supplementary provisions give enforcement dates and replace earlier Finance Ministry ordinances; the translation cites the Official Gazette of April 12, 1941.

subfiles.title: Income Tax Law of Japan, Law No. 24 of 1940 (selected articles)
subfiles.about: Selected provisions define taxable income, exemptions, calculations, rates, deductions, declarations, and Income Investigation Committees.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt distinguishes classified and composite income tax, defines taxable income and exemptions, and specifies calculations, thresholds, rates, and household deductions. It sets out taxpayer declarations and government assessment procedures. Later articles govern the election, tenure, voting, and deliberations of Income Investigation Committees; a closing note states that articles 67–110 are omitted.
